heros.infro: Diogenes the Cynic (c. 412-323 B.C.) of Sinope was an ascetic Greek philosopher who lived abstemiously, most likely begging and stealing for his livelihood, and thought there was no such thing as an honest man. He was called Kynos (Greek for dog) for his lifestyle and contrary nature.  It is from this word for dog that we derive the word cynic.  He was a student of the philosopher Antisthenes, himself a student of Socrates.  The principles of their philosophy of Cynicism included self-sufficiency, living by personal example, exposing the falsehood of conventional thinking, exposing vice and deceit, and living according to nature.
heros.name: Diogenes
